$schema_note: Destination specs read by export.py and check.py and by the Director for the destination question. width/height are the export frame; fps null = keep the source rate (made constant); max_duration_s null = no cap; lufs/true_peak_dbtp are loudness targets; safe_zones are the percentages of the frame a platform's UI covers; audio false = export without an audio track.

instagram-reels.label: Instagram Reels
instagram-reels.notes: The bottom fifth holds the caption/CTA row and the right column the action icons; keep burned text above them.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.notes: Under 60 s performs best; the UI overlay is larger than Reels.

youtube-shorts.label: YouTube Shorts
youtube-shorts.notes: 60 s is the classic cap; up to 180 s accepted. Title overlay sits at the top.

youtube.label: YouTube
youtube.notes: Keep the source frame rate; 4K is fine when the source is 4K. Prefer a sidecar SRT over burned captions.

x.label: X / Twitter
x.notes: Autoplays muted in the feed; captions carry the message.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.notes: Square takes the most feed space; muted autoplay.

facebook.label: Facebook
facebook.notes: 4:5 is the tallest feed format; muted autoplay.

whatsapp-status.label: WhatsApp status
whatsapp-status.notes: Heavily recompressed; keep text large and the file small.

website-loop.label: Website hero loop
website-loop.notes: No audio track, small file, seamless loop; 10–20 s is plenty.

presentation.label: Presentation / embed
presentation.notes: Plays in a room through speakers; speech-first loudness.
